about.title: Every family deserves restful nights.
about.bio_1: Hello, I'm Giulia! Italian mum of two living in London, I am a certified infant sleep coach. I believe baby sleep is not a matter of luck — it is a science shaped by routines, environment, and small but powerful adjustments.
about.bio_2: At « Maman Giulia », I look at your child's entire daily life, well beyond the hours spent in the crib. I address feeding, daytime activities, recurring challenges, and much more. My approach is gentle, evidence-based, and deeply respectful of your family's unique rhythm.
about.bio_3: I'm here to help you find your energy back and build a sustainable routine — so you can focus on the joy of watching your children grow.

quiz.title: Test yourself on baby sleep
quiz.subtitle: 3 situations. What do you do? We'll tell you what you need to know.
quiz.result_label: What this article will give you
quiz.result_subtitle: Based on your answers, this article has the concrete answers you need:
quiz.result_all_good: Your instincts are good. To go even further, here's our reference article:

questions.text: Your baby has been awake for 1h15. They're yawning and starting to stare into space. What do you do?
answers: I offer a toy — they don't really look tired yet
I start the sleep routine right away
I wait until they cry to be sure they're ready

questions.text: A relative advises you to keep your baby awake longer in the evening so they sleep better at night. What do you do?
answers: I try it — a more tired baby should sleep more deeply
I keep to the wake window even in the evening — overtired babies sleep worse, not better
I extend it slightly and observe over a few days

questions.text: It's 7:30pm. Baby has been crying for 45 minutes, inconsolable. Clean nappy, just fed. What do you do?
answers: I turn on the TV or a light-up toy to distract them
I dim the lights, reduce noise, and hold them close
I bring them to the living room where there's people and activity

questions.text: Your baby has been crying every evening at the same time for a week. Clean nappy, not hungry, nothing works. What do you think is happening?
answers: My milk supply drops in the evening — they're hungry
Their nervous system is overloaded by the day's stimulations
They're teething or may have a food allergy

questions.text: Your 3-day-old is asking for the breast every 30 minutes tonight. It doesn't seem like real hunger. What do you do?
answers: I limit feeds — a routine needs to be established from the start
I let them feed as much as they want, even if it lasts all night
I give a pacifier to space out the feeds a little

questions.text: It's the 2nd night at home. Your baby, calm yesterday, refuses to be put down and keeps asking for the breast. What do you think?
answers: They've picked up a bad habit in just one night
It's a normal mechanism — they're stimulating milk production and seeking contact
My milk hasn't come in yet — we may need to supplement

questions.text: Your baby is 6 weeks old and nights are still chaotic. A friend says: 'It's their temperament — some babies are just like that.' What do you do?
answers: I accept it — they're probably highly sensitive, nothing to be done
I put a consistent routine in place and observe for 2 weeks
I look for information about high-need babies to adapt my approach

questions.text: For 3 weeks, you've been putting your baby to bed at varying times depending on your evening. Nights remain unpredictable. What do you do?
answers: I adapt to their rhythm — forcing a fixed time would stress them
I set a bedtime and a routine, even if imperfect, and I stick to it
I wait until they're a little older to establish a routine

questions.text: Your 4-week-old often has gas, cries after feeds, and has fragmented nights. Your first thought goes to…
answers: The evening routine — maybe it's not consistent enough
Their gut and feeding — digestive balance directly affects sleep
Their temperament — some babies just have a harder time digesting

questions.text: You're breastfeeding and your baby often has gas and cries after feeds. You first look at…
answers: Their routine — maybe they're overstimulated before feeds
My diet — what I eat passes into the milk and can affect their comfort
Nothing special — gas is normal in all newborns
